tagline: Building software that empowers organizations to effectively integrate their data, decisions, and operations at scale
hero_kpi_rationale: Palantir positions AIP as its primary growth vector, integrating generative AI directly into client operations through secure workflows, making it the key driver of its current trajectory

kpis.name: AI-inclusive deals share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of new contracts that include generative AI capabilities via AIP.
kpis.description: In 2025, 60% of new contracts include AIP, demonstrating massive integration of generative AI into commercial and government client operational workflows.
kpis.signal: 60% of new deals include AIP: rapid adoption of AI in client operations.

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by the company during the year.
kpis.description: Revenue increases from $2.9B in 2024 to $4.5B in 2025, driven by commercial expansion and AIP adoption.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Margin after cost of services, before overhead expenses.
kpis.description: Gross margin improves from 80% to 82% between 2024 and 2025, supported by platform scalability and AIP ramp-up.
kpis.signal: 82% gross margin: typical of a high-end SaaS software provider.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.description: Operating profit increases from $310M to $1.4B in 2025, representing a 31% margin versus 11% in 2024.
kpis.signal: 31% operating margin: a rare threshold in software following strong growth.

kpis.name: R&D (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Share of revenue invested in research and development.
kpis.description: Despite growth, Palantir maintains high R&D spending to advance AIP and the Ontology, with a slight decrease as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.signal: R&D at 18%: intensive but controlled, typical of innovative tech leaders.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Headcount increases from 5.4K to 6.5K between 2024 and 2025, reflecting active hiring to support commercial and technical operations.
kpis.signal: +20% headcount: sustained expansion to support growth.

kpis.name: Number of customers
kpis.explanation: Number of customer organizations over the last 12 months.
kpis.description: Customer count increases from 711 in 2024 to 954 in 2025, showing significant expansion in both commercial and government sectors.
kpis.signal: +243 new customers in one year: accelerated market penetration.

kpis.name: Average revenue top 20 customers
kpis.explanation: Average revenue generated by each of the top 20 customers.
kpis.description: Average revenue per top customer increases from $64.6M to $93.9M in 2025, indicating strong expansion within existing relationships.
kpis.signal: 45% growth among large accounts: evidence of successful upsell.

risks.title: Customer contract dependency and termination risk
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly states that many contracts are subject to termination for convenience clauses. The total value of remaining contracts is a key metric, but its reliability depends on the absence of terminations and exercise of options, representing a significant risk to revenue predictability.

risks.title: Impact of global macroeconomic conditions
risks.score_rationale: The risk related to macroeconomic trends is clearly identified as affecting the company and its clients. It includes geopolitical tensions, interest rates, monetary policy, and currency fluctuations, directly impacting operations and results.

risks.title: Geopolitical tensions risk
risks.score_rationale: Although the company minimizes the current impact of conflicts (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East), it acknowledges that escalation could negatively affect its operations. This risk is specifically mentioned and closely monitored.

risks.title: Foreign exchange rate fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: The document details how exchange rate variations, particularly against the Euro and British Pound, can negatively affect revenues and expenses of non-U.S. clients and subsidiaries. This risk is explicitly named and explained.

risks.title: Macroeconomic impact on customers
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes that macroeconomic conditions affect the company's customers, potentially leading to negative impacts on new customer acquisition, contract renewals, and collections.

risks.title: Significant stock-based compensation expenses
risks.score_rationale: The document repeatedly mentions expenses related to stock options, particularly in non-GAAP measure reconciliations. While non-cash, these expenses are significant and affect reported profitability.

ai_positioning.summary: PLTR does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing. The information provided focuses primarily on financials, operations, and corporate governance, with no significant reference to AI.
